Farmer–Citizen Movement: Netherlands. The Farmer–Citizen Movement (Dutch: BoerBurgerBeweging [buːrˈbʏrɣərbəˌʋeːɣɪŋ]; BBB) is an agrarian and right-wing populist political party in the Netherlands.

Juche: North Korea. Juche, officially the Juche idea, is a name of the official ideology of North Korea and its ruling Workers' Party of Korea (WPK).

Manchester Arena bombing: United Kingdom. On 22 May 2017, twenty-two people were killed and 1,017 injured in an Islamic terrorist suicide bombing at Manchester Arena in Manchester, England.

Hyderabad State: Urdu. The state was ruled from 1724 to 1948 by the Nizam, who was initially a viceroy of the Mughal Empire in the Deccan.

Yugoslavia: Serbo-Croatian. Yugoslavia (lit. 'Land of the South Slavs') was a country in Central Europe and the Balkans that existed from 1918 to 1992.
Who is credited with discovering Big Bang?
Big Bang: Georges Lemaître. The Big Bang is a physical theory that describes how the universe expanded from an initial state of high density and temperature.
Succeeding Sani Abacha upon his death, this Nigerian general steered the country to multiparty elections and handed power to Olusegun Obasanjo in 1999 — who was he?
Abdulsalami Abubakar (born 13 June 1942) is a retired Nigerian army general who served as the military head of state of Nigeria from 1998 to 1999.

This Russian politician served as personal bodyguard to President Putin before rising to lead special forces that oversaw the 2014 annexation of Crimea, later becoming Deputy Defense Minister — who is he?
Aleksey Dyumin (born 28 August 1972) is a Russian politician serving as Secretary of the State Council since 2024.

Before he ever entered Parliament, this Welshman was a miners' union firebrand in the 1926 general strike — but he's best remembered for spearheading the creation of the British National Health Service as Attlee's Minister of Health. Who was he?

Aneurin Bevan (15 November 1897 - 6 July 1960) was a Welsh Labour Party politician, noted for spearheading the creation of the British National Health Service during his tenure as Minister of Health in Clement Attlee's government.

This Burmese politician and diplomat served as State Counsellor from 2016 to 2021 and was instrumental in Myanmar's transition from military rule toward democracy. She's been the general secretary of the National League for Democracy since the party's founding in 1988 — who is she?
Aung San Suu Kyi (born 19 June 1945) is a Burmese politician, diplomat and author who served as State Counsellor of Myanmar and Minister of Foreign Affairs from 2016 to 2021.
Once Lord Mayor of Dublin, this Fianna Fáil leader became the second-longest-serving Taoiseach before resigning in 2008 amid the Mahon Tribunal's revelations — who is he?
Bertie Ahern (born 12 September 1951) is an Irish former Fianna Fil politician who served as Taoiseach from 1997 to 2008, and as Leader of Fianna Fil from 1994 to 2008.

Born to a Syrian family and raised Muslim, this Argentine president converted to Catholicism to pursue politics and ran the country for a full decade under his namesake brand of Peronism — who was he?
Carlos Menem (Spanish; 2 July 1930 - 14 February 2021) was an Argentine politician who served as the president of Argentina for ten years, from 1989 to 1999.

Nominated by President George H. W. Bush in 1991 to succeed Thurgood Marshall, this associate justice of the U.S. Supreme Court is the second African American to serve on the bench and the second longest-serving justice in history. Who is he?
Clarence Thomas (born June 23, 1948) is an American lawyer and jurist who has served since 1991 as an associate justice of the Supreme Court of the United States.
This category of evil supernatural being, believed in since possibly the Paleolithic age, appears across folklore, religion, and occultism worldwide — name it?
Demon is an evil or malevolent supernatural entity.
Widowed in 1945, this longest-serving American first lady reinvented her role and championed the text of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights at the UN — who was she?
Eleanor Roosevelt (October 11, 1884 - November 7, 1962) was an American political figure, diplomat, and activist.

Rising from a lowly one-year-volunteer enlistee to Field Marshal — a first in his army — this Wehrmacht general was later convicted of war crimes by courts in both the Soviet Union and West Germany — who was he?

Ferdinand Schörner (12 June 1892 - 2 July 1973) was a German military commander and convicted war criminal, who held the rank of Generalfeldmarschall (Field Marshal) in the Wehrmacht of Nazi Germany during World War II.
Which American politician, a convicted felon, served less than a year representing New York's 3rd district before being expelled from Congress in 2023?
George Santos (born July 22, 1988) is an American former politician and convicted felon.

Born to a farming family, this Indian politician served as chief minister of Karnataka before a roughly 11-month stint as prime minister of India in 1996-97, and has led his regional party since 1999. Who is he?
H. D. Deve Gowda (born 18 May 1933) is an Indian politician who served as the prime minister of India for nearly 11 months, from 1996 to 1997.
A leader of the army's 'Control Faction' in the 1930s, this officer became Japan's wartime prime minister in 1941; his rule was marked by widespread state violence — who is he?
Hideki Tojo (30 December 1884 - 23 December 1948) was a Japanese military officer and politician who served as Prime Minister of Japan from 1941 to 1944 during World War II.
Once rated Ukraine's second-richest man, this Ukrainian-born Israeli billionaire co-founded PrivatBank in 1992 and later served as a regional governor during the early war with Russia — who is he?
Ihor Kolomoyskyi (born 13 February 1963) is a Ukrainian-born Israeli billionaire businessman, once considered the leading oligarch in Ukraine.
Sent to take refuge on the Bass Rock as a boy after his escort was attacked, this youngest son of Robert III ruled the Scots from 1406 to 1437 — who was he?
James I of Scotland (late July 1394 - 21 February 1437) was King of Scots from 1406 to 1437.

Born in Centreville, Mississippi and educated at Vanderbilt, UVA Law, and Oxford, this Republican has served as Louisiana's junior U.S. Senator since 2017 after 17 years as the state's Treasurer — name this politician?
John Kennedy (Louisiana politician) (born November 21, 1951) is an American politician and attorney who has served as the junior United States senator from Louisiana since 2017.
A WWI U-boat commander taken prisoner by the British in 1918, he later briefly became Nazi Germany's head of state after Hitler's suicide — who is it?

Karl Dönitz (16 September 1891 - 24 December 1980) was a German naval officer and politician who briefly succeeded Adolf Hitler as the head of state of Nazi Germany after the latter's suicide during the World War II in April 1945.
Widow of warlord Toyotomi Hideyoshi, this Buddhist nun founded a temple in Kyoto and monitored daimyo families held hostage at Osaka Castle — who was she?
Kōdai-in (died October 17, 1624), formerly known as Nene, One, Nei, was an aristocrat and Buddhist nun, founder of the temple Kdai-ji in Kyoto, Japan.
A Spanish Navy officer who fought in the Rif War and Civil War before rising through Franco's government, he was handpicked as the dictator's successor as head of government — who is he?
Luis Carrero Blanco (Spanish; 4 March 1904 - 20 December 1973) was a Spanish Navy officer and politician.
This retired U.S. Army general served as the 20th chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff from 2019 to 2023, after earlier serving as the Army's 39th chief of staff — who is he?
Mark Milley (born 20 June 1958) is a retired United States Army general who served as the 20th chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff from 2019 to 2023.
She served as deputy First Minister of Northern Ireland from 2020 to 2022 before rising to First Minister in 2024 — who is she?
Michelle O'Neill (ne Doris; born 10 January 1977) is an Irish politician who has been First Minister of Northern Ireland since February 2024 and Vice President of Sinn Fin since 2018.
This former footballer and journalist represented the Heingang constituency and rose to become Manipur's 12th Chief Minister, serving from 2017 to 2025 — who is he?

N. Biren Singh (Meitei; born 1 January 1961) is an Indian politician, former footballer and journalist who served as the 12th Chief Minister of Manipur from 2017 to 2025 as a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party.
This Indian politician has served as Minister of Road Transport & Highways since 2014, becoming the only person to hold that single portfolio for three consecutive terms — who is he?
Nitin Gadkari (born 27 May 1957) is an Indian politician who is serving as the 40th Minister of Road Transport & Highways since 2014.
Also known for the character Professor Kranz, this Italian actor and writer penned satirical books and became famous for grotesque comic creations, including a meek accountant — who is he?
Paolo Villaggio (30 December 1932 - 3 July 2017) was an Italian actor, comedian, film director, and writer.
Whether offered alone or in groups, as part of a set ritual or spontaneously, this act of communication with a deity can seek intercession, give thanks, or offer praise — what is it called?
Prayer is an invocation or act that seeks to activate a rapport with an object of worship through deliberate communication.
After leading the Congress to victory in the 2023 state election that toppled the incumbent Bharat Rashtra Samithi, which politician became the current Chief Minister of Telangana?
Revanth Reddy (born 8 November 1969) is an Indian politician who is serving as the second and current Chief Minister of Telangana.
Born in London to a Pakistani family and once a practicing solicitor, this Labour politician represented Tooting in Parliament before becoming the city's mayor in 2016 — who is he?
Sadiq Khan (born 8 October 1970) is a British politician serving as the third and current strategic authority mayor for London since 2016.
Known by the honorific 'Bangabandhu,' this Bengali politician led his country to independence and served as its founding president before being assassinated in a 1975 coup — who is he?

Sheikh Mujibur Rahman (17 March 1920 - 15 August 1975), also known as Mujib or by the honorific Bangabandhu, was a Bangladeshi politician, revolutionary, statesman, activist and diarist who was the founding president of Bangladesh.
Once a mere province under the Bahmani Kingdom, it broke free in 1490 to become one of the Deccan's most powerful states — until Aurangzeb's Mughals swallowed it in 1686. What kingdom was it?
Sultanate of Bijapur was an early modern kingdom in the western Deccan and South India, ruled by the Muslim Adil Shahi (or Adilshahi) dynasty.

Elected king by Ostrogothic nobles in 541 after his two predecessors were murdered for trying to surrender, this skilled commander reversed the tide of the Gothic War and clawed back nearly all of Italy by 543. Who is he?
Totila (died 1 July 552), was the penultimate King of the Ostrogoths, reigning from 541 to 552.
This Russian right-wing populist politician led a nationalist party from its 1992 founding until his death in 2022, twice serving as deputy chairman of the State Duma. Who is he?

Vladimir Zhirinovsky (25 April 1946 - 6 April 2022) was a Russian right-wing populist politician who served as the leader of the Liberal Democratic Party of Russia (LDPR) from its creation in 1992 until his death in 2022.
Born in Virginia and holding a Ph.D. from Johns Hopkins, this 28th president led the nation through World War I and lent his name to a foreign-policy doctrine — who was he?
Woodrow Wilson (December 28, 1856 - February 3, 1924) was the 28th president of the United States, serving from 1913 to 1921.

Cambodian–Vietnamese War: 1978–89 conflict between Vietnam and the Khmer Rouge.

Claudius: Roman emperor from AD 41 to 54.
United under King Burebista in 82 BC and centered on Transylvania, this ancient kingdom fell after Roman conquest in AD 106, its capital Sarmizegetusa Regia destroyed — what was this land called?
Dacia: Ancient kingdom in Southeastern Europe (168 BC – 106 AD)

Refusing to carry a weapon because of his faith, this WWII combat medic saved an estimated 75 men during the Battle of Okinawa and became the first conscientious objector awarded the Medal of Honor — who was he, later portrayed by Andrew Garfield?
Desmond Doss: US soldier and Medal of Honor recipient (1919–2006)

Organized by the Irish Republican Brotherhood and lasting six days in April 1916, this armed insurrection aimed to end British rule and saw sixteen of its leaders executed — what was this uprising called?

Easter Rising: 1916 armed insurrection in Ireland. The Easter Rising (Irish: Éirí Amach na Cásca), also known as the Easter Rebellion, was an armed insurrection in Ireland during Easter Week in April 1916.

Ezekiel: Prophet in the Abrahamic religions.

Frances Shand Kydd: Mother of Diana, Princess of Wales (1936–2004)
Born in Punta Arenas, this left-wing student-protest leader rose from the Chamber of Deputies to become president of Chile in 2022 — who is it?

Gabriel Boric: President of Chile from 2022 to 2026. Gabriel Boric Font (Spanish: [ɡaˈβɾjel ˈβoɾitʃ ˈfont];; born 11 February 1986) is a Chilean politician who served as President of Chile from 2022 to 2026.
Serving as Italy's president from 2006 to 2015, this former Communist Party member became the country's longest-serving head of state and the first ever re-elected to the office — who was he?
Giorgio Napolitano: President of Italy from 2006 to 2015. In 2005, Napolitano was appointed a senator for life in Italy by then president Carlo Azeglio Ciampi.

In May 1980, student-led protests in a South Korean city rose against Chun Doo-hwan's coup and martial law, only to be crushed by the military at a cost of hundreds to thousands of lives — what is this event called?
Gwangju Uprising: 1980 anti-government protest in South Korea.
Though overshadowed by the more famous Spitfire, this RAF fighter actually inflicted 60 percent of the Luftwaffe's losses during the Battle of Britain — which 1930s aircraft?
Hawker Hurricane: British fighter aircraft of the 1930s and 40s.
Ruled from the ancient city of Zafar near modern Sanaa, this kingdom of Yemen's southern highlands eventually swallowed up its neighbors Saba', Qataban, and Hadramaut — which polity?
Himyar: Former kingdom in ancient Yemen. Himyar was a polity in the southern highlands of Yemen, as well as the name of the region which it claimed.
Beginning with Napoleon's return from exile on Elba and ending with the second restoration of Louis XVIII after Waterloo, what name is given to this roughly 110-day period in 1815?
Hundred Days: 1815 period of the Napoleonic Wars.
Whose name means 'he will laugh,' this biblical patriarch was the son of Abraham and Sarah and the father of Jacob and Esau, living to age 180 — who was he?

Isaac: Biblical patriarch, son of Abraham and Sarah. Isaac first appears in the Torah, in which he is the son of Abraham and Sarah, the father of Jacob and Esau, and the grandfather of the twelve tribes of Israel.

According to the Book of Kings, this wife of King Ahab of Israel promoted Baal worship and met her end thrown from a window and devoured by dogs — who is she?
Jezebel: Biblical figure; Phoenician princess and wife of Ahab.
Trained as an aeronautical engineer and mathematics professor, this Spanish politician served as the EU's top diplomat and a European Commission vice-president from 2019 to 2024 — who is he?
Elected in 2019 with over 72 percent of the vote as an anti-corruption independent, this law professor became Tunisia's fifth president — who is he?
Kais Saied: President of Tunisia since 2019. As president, Saied has overseen democratic backsliding, as he has repressed the political opposition and dissidents in Tunisia.
On May 2, 2011, SEAL Team Six carried out Operation Neptune Spear at a compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan, ending a manhunt that began with the war in Afghanistan — what event was this?
Killing of Osama bin Laden: 2011 U.S. military operation in Abbottabad, Pakistan.
In Arthurian legend, this enchantress figure gifts Excalibur to the king, raises the knight Lancelot, and later helps carry the dying king to Avalon — who or what is she?
Lady of the Lake: Sorceress in Arthurian legend. As either single character or multiple ones, the figure of the Lady of the Lake often appears in various roles in the works of modern culture.

Shaped by liberal ideas and the non-aggression principle, this political philosophy prizes liberty and personal sovereignty above all, holding you may live as you choose so long as you don't force or defraud others — what is it?
Libertarianism: Political philosophy based on liberty. Different categorizations have been used to distinguish these various forms of libertarianism.
A Burma Campaign veteran regarded as the founder of the Bangladesh Armed Forces, he served as commander-in-chief of the Bangladesh Forces in 1971 — who was this four-star general?
M. A. G. Osmani: Bangladeshi military general & revolutionary (1918–1984)

Educated in Moscow and a veteran of several wars, this military officer was the eldest son of the Chinese Communist Party's founding chairman, before he was killed by a U.S. napalm strike in the Korean War. Who was he?
Mao Anying: Chinese military officer and son of Mao Zedong. Mao Anying (Chinese: 毛岸英; pinyin: Máo Ànyīng; 24 October 1922 – 25 November 1950) was a Chinese military officer.
Leader of the People's Mojahedin Organization of Iran from 1979, which Iranian revolutionary vanished shortly before the 2003 invasion of Iraq, leaving his wife as the group's public face?

A former agricultural engineer who once served as mayor of Amarah, this politician rose to become Iraq's prime minister from 2022 to 2026. Who is he?
Mohammed Shia' al-Sudani: Prime Minister of Iraq from 2022 to 2026.

Ninety-five Theses: Disputation by Martin Luther on indulgences.
Having joined the Italian resistance as a teenager in World War II, this journalist grew famous for fierce interviews with the likes of Henry Kissinger, Golda Meir, and the Shah of Iran — who is she?
Oriana Fallaci: Italian journalist and author (1929–2006)

This semi-nomadic Turkic people controlled the steppes of southeastern Europe and Crimea in the 9th and 10th centuries, waging war against the early Rus' state for over two hundred years — who were they?
Pechenegs: Extinct Turkic people. The Pechenegs or Patzinaks, were a semi-nomadic Turkic people from Central Asia who spoke the Pecheneg language.

Head of the Catholic Church for nearly 32 years — the longest verified reign in history — this pontiff convened a council that defined papal infallibility before declaring himself a 'prisoner' after Rome's capture in 1870 — who was he?
Pope Pius IX: Head of the Catholic Church from 1846 to 1878.
A war correspondent in Afghanistan and Angola in the 1980s, this Oxford-educated Polish statesman later became his country's Foreign Minister and, since 2025, also Deputy Prime Minister — who is he?
Radosław Sikorski: Polish politician and journalist (born 1963)
This Congress politician led his party to victory in the 2023 election and became the second Chief Minister of Telangana — who is he?
Revanth Reddy: Chief Minister of Telangana (born 1969)
Valedictorian of Plains High School in Georgia, this American first lady became a lifelong champion of mental health and women's rights — who was she?
Rosalynn Carter: First Lady of the United States from 1977 to 1981.
In October 2025, she became the first woman ever to serve as Prime Minister of Japan — who is she?
Sanae Takaichi: Prime Minister of Japan since 2025. Takaichi's administration has consistently polled high in approval ratings.
A close friend of Stalin who rose to lead the Communist Party in Leningrad, his 1934 assassination at the Smolny Institute became Stalin's pretext for the Great Purge — who was he?
Sergei Kirov: Soviet politician and revolutionary (1886–1934)

Siege of Turin: 1706 battle of the War of the Spanish Succession. The Siege of Turin, June to September 1706, took place during the War of the Spanish Succession.

Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani: Emir of Qatar since 2013.
Brother of King Henry VIII's third wife, this nobleman married the king's widow Catherine Parr in 1547 while sparring with his own brother for influence over the young King Edward VI — who was he?
Thomas Seymour, 1st Baron Seymour of Sudeley

This Indian politician served as Maharashtra's 19th chief minister from 2019 to 2022 while also editing a newspaper for over a decade — who is he?

Posthumously awarded India's highest military honor, the Param Vir Chakra, this army captain died fighting Pakistani troops at Point 4875 during the Kargil War in 1999 — who is he?

Beginning with the 1916 death of Yuan Shikai, this chaotic decade-plus in Chinese history saw the country splinter under rival military cliques until Sun Yat-sen's Nationalists challenged the Beijing government for legitimacy — which period?
Warlord Era: Period in the history of the Republic of China (1916–1928)
The only Democrat elected president during the Republican-dominated Progressive Era, he steered the U.S. through World War I and championed the League of Nations — which 28th president was he?
Woodrow Wilson: President of the United States from 1913 to 1921.

This Polish politician served two stints as justice minister — one ending under PM Mateusz Morawiecki in 2023 — while also holding the prosecutor general post and championing an anti-corruption crusade — who is he?
Who among these was born first?
Soichiro Honda (born 1906) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was born earliest?
Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four. Henry Vaughan (1621 – 23 April 1695) was a Welsh metaphysical poet, author and translator writing in English, and a medical physician.
Which of these four began earliest?
Messerschmitt Bf 109 (founded 1937) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was established earliest?
C (programming language) (founded 1972) is the earliest of the four. C is a general-purpose programming language created in the 1970s by Dennis Ritchie.
Which one below is best known as a physicist?
Max Born is a physicist. During World War I, Born was originally placed as a radio operator, but his specialist knowledge led to his being moved to research duties on sound ranging.
Pick the chemist from these four.
Antoine Lavoisier is a chemist. It is generally accepted that Lavoisier's great accomplishments in chemistry stem largely from his changing the science from a qualitative to a quantitative one.
What is the atomic number of Oxygen?
Oxygen is a chemical element; it has the symbol O and its atomic number is 8.
In what year was Werner Heisenberg born?
Werner Heisenberg: Heisenberg published his Umdeutung paper in 1925, a major reinterpretation of old quantum theory.
In what year was Glutathione discovered?
Glutathione (GSH,) is a tripeptide made of the amino acids glutamate, cysteine, and glycine.
In what year was Morphine discovered?
Morphine, formerly known as morphium, is an opiate found naturally in opium, a dark brown resin produced by drying the latex of opium poppies (Papaver somniferum).
Acetylcysteine: Pfizer. It has been used to treat lactobezoar in infants.
In which country is Embraer E-Jet family based?
Embraer E-Jet family: Brazil. The E-Jet was designed to complement Embraer's earlier ERJ family, the company's first jet-powered regional aircraft.
Who is credited with discovering Radon?
Radon: Friedrich Ernst Dorn. Radon is a chemical element; it has symbol Rn and atomic number 86.
Who is credited with discovering Tautavel Man?
Tautavel Man: Henry de Lumley. Tautavel Man refers to the archaic humans which—from approximately 550,000 to 400,000 years ago—inhabited the Caune de l’Arago, a limestone cave in Tautavel, France.
Who is credited with discovering MDMA?
MDMA: Anton Köllisch. MDMA was first synthesized in 1912 by Merck chemist Anton Köllisch.
Though the word is often dropped from its name, invasive ductal carcinoma — the most common breast cancer — technically falls under this broader glandular cancer classification — what is it?
De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter
Adenocarcinoma (AC) is a type of cancer made of cells from glands.
Formed naturally around volcanic vents and on burning coal dumps, this soluble white crystalline salt serves as both a fertilizer and a food additive — what's the compound with formula NH4Cl?
Ammonium chloride is an inorganic chemical compound with the chemical formula NH4Cl, also written as Cl.

This superfamily of tailless Old World primates, native to sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia and more closely related to Old World monkeys than New World ones, includes humans among its members — what's this group called?
Ape (hominoids), are a superfamily of Old World simians native to sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia.
Found throughout North America from Canada to northern Mexico, this sea eagle has two subspecies and forms a pair with the white-tailed eagle—name it.
Bald eagle (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) is a bird of prey found in North America.

Found mainly in New Guinea, which family of forty-four species — the males famous for extravagant, elaborate plumage sprouting from their beaks, wings, tails, or heads — is confined largely to dense rainforest?
Bird-of-paradise are members of the family Paradisaeidae of the order Passeriformes.
This cabbage-family vegetable, whose large dark-green flowering head is eaten as food, closely resembles its paler relative cauliflower — name it?
Native to nearly all of South America, this semiaquatic, grass-munching cousin of the guinea pig holds the title of largest living rodent — what is it?
Capybara (Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris) is the largest living rodent, native to all countries in South America except Chile.

The smallest recognized dog breed in the world, this Mexican toy breed has large erect ears and a rounded skull, and its genes carry a trace of pre-Columbian indigenous American dog ancestry — which breed?

Chihuahua (dog breed) is a Mexican breed of toy dog and the smallest recognized dog breed in the world. It is primarily kept as a companion animal and is characterized by its compact size, large erect ears, and rounded skull.
This digestive condition refers to swelling or inflammation of the large intestine, and can be acute and short-lived or a long-term, chronic issue — what is it called?
Colitis is swelling or inflammation of the large intestine (colon). It broadly fits into the category of digestive diseases.
Together with birds, this order of predatory reptiles is one of only two survivors of the ancient Archosauria — and it lumps together alligators, caimans, and gharials. What is it?
Crocodilia is an order of semiaquatic, predatory reptiles that are known as crocodilians.
A colorless liquid that's a workhorse solvent for chemical reactions, this compound is officially odorless — yet degraded samples reek of fish thanks to a dimethylamine impurity; what is it?
Dimethylformamide is an organic compound with the chemical formula HCON(CH3)2.

This scientific and engineering discipline uses transistors, diodes, and integrated circuits to control and amplify the flow of electric current, converting between forms like AC to DC. What is the field called?

Electronics is a scientific and engineering discipline that studies and applies the principles of physics to design, create, and operate devices that manipulate electrons and other electrically charged particles.
They're a tiny minority by headcount among living things, yet their larger bodies make their combined biomass dwarf that of bacteria and archaea — what membrane-bound-nucleus group is this?
Eukaryote are the domain Eukaryota or Eukarya, organisms whose cells have a membrane-bound nucleus.
Systematically named methanal and carrying the formula CH2O, this pungent gas turns up in particle board, disinfectants, and lab specimen jars — what is it?

Formaldehyde (for-, US also fr-) (systematic name methanal) is a pungent colorless gas mainly used in the production of industrial resins, such as for particle board, coatings, plastics, pulp, paper, synthetic fibers, and textiles.
The tallest living land animal and the largest ruminant on Earth, this African mammal's closest living relative is the shorter-necked okapi — name the animal?
Giraffe (genus Giraffa) are large African hoofed mammals.
Named for a flattened, laterally extended head shape called a cephalofoil, with eyes placed at each end of the T, this family of sharks includes species mostly grouped in one genus — which sharks?

Hammerhead shark are a group of sharks that form the family Sphyrnidae, named for the unusual and distinctive form of their heads, which are flattened and laterally extended into a cephalofoil (a T-shape or "hammer").
This perennial root vegetable, a relative of mustard, wasabi, broccoli, and cabbage, is grated and used worldwide as a pungent spice and condiment — what plant is it?
This contagious bacterial skin infection most often shows up as yellowish crusts on a child's face, arms, or legs, and spreads easily in crowded day cares and contact sports — what is it?
Impetigo is a contagious bacterial infection that involves the superficial skin.
Director of Columbia's Center for Sustainable Development, which economist led the United Nations Millennium Project's work on the Millennium Development Goals?
Jeffrey Sachs (SAKS; born November 5, 1954) is an American economist and public policy analyst.
Native to Central and South American rainforests, this frugivorous nocturnal mammal related to raccoons and coatis shares its 'honey bear' nickname with an unrelated species — which animal?
Kinkajou (/kkdu/; Potos flavus) is a mammal of the family Procyonidae, a relative to olingos, coatis, raccoons, and the ringtail and cacomistle.
An indoor watchdog by tradition, this dog breed originated high in Tibet — which non-sporting breed is it?
Lhasa Apso is a non-sporting dog breed originating in Tibet.
Caused by a compromised lymphatic system, this condition raises infection risk in affected tissue and is treated with compression and massage rather than water pills — what is it?
Lymphedema (USA), lymphoedema (UK) also known as lymphatic edema (US)/oedema (UK), is a condition of localized swelling caused by a compromised lymphatic system.
This German-British theoretical physicist won a Nobel Prize for his statistical interpretation of the wavefunction, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics. Who is he?
Max Born (11 December 1882 - 5 January 1970) was a German-British theoretical physicist who was instrumental in the development of quantum mechanics.
This unit of time, normally equal to 60 seconds, can rarely stretch to 61 seconds under the UTC time standard because of a leap second — what is it?
Minute (symbol: min) is a unit of time defined as equal to 60 seconds.
Found from Africa to Southeast Asia, this snake genus contains the 'true cobras' as opposed to look-alikes like the king cobra — which genus?
Naja is a genus of venomous elapid snakes commonly known as cobras (or "true cobras").
What's the name for the scholarly study and collection of coins, paper money, tokens and medals — though by its rules, cigarettes traded in prison don't count?
Numismatics is the study or collection of currency, including coins, tokens, paper money, medals, and related objects.
Inflammation of the enzyme-and-hormone-producing organ behind the stomach, it comes in acute and chronic forms and can lead to diabetes — what is this condition?
Pancreatitis is a condition characterized by inflammation of the pancreas.
This Belgian-British microbiologist helped discover the Ebola virus in 1976 and led the fight against that first recorded outbreak before becoming a pioneering AIDS researcher — who is he?
Peter Piot (born 17 February 1949) is a Belgian-British microbiologist known for his research into Ebola and AIDS.

There are only five of these convex, regular three-dimensional shapes — including the cube, tetrahedron, and icosahedron — where every face is an identical regular polygon. What are these shapes called?
Platonic solid is a convex, regular polyhedron in three-dimensional Euclidean space.
Discovered in 1915 and too faint to see with the naked eye, which small, dim star, orbiting its two brighter neighbors once every 550,000 years, is our closest stellar neighbor after the Sun?
Proxima Centauri is the nearest star to Earth after the Sun, located 4.25 light-years (1.3 parsecs) away in the southern constellation of Centaurus.
Physicists denote this stretching of light's wavelength — caused by relative motion, gravity, or cosmic expansion — with the symbol z; its opposite is called blueshift. What is it?
Redshift is an increase in the wavelength, or equivalently, a decrease in the frequency, of electromagnetic radiation (such as light).

Grown mainly from Eastern and Northern Europe into Russia, this cold-tolerant grain crop is a member of the wheat tribe and its vigorous growth suppresses weeds while providing early forage for animals — name it?
Rye (Secale cereale) is a grass grown extensively as a grain, a cover crop and a forage crop.
This Russian politician has served as mayor of Moscow since 2010, after earlier stints as a regional governor, head of the presidential administration, and deputy prime minister — who is he?
Sergey Sobyanin (born 21 June 1958) is a Russian politician, serving as the 3rd mayor of Moscow since 21 October 2010.
Known by such nicknames as 'sour dock' and 'spinach dock,' this tangy Eurasian herb thrives wild in grasslands and is often used as a leaf vegetable — which plant?
Sorrel (Rumex acetosa) is a perennial herbaceous plant in the family Polygonaceae.
The fifth most common element on Earth, this multivalent nonmetal usually turns up in sulfide and sulfate minerals and is a bright yellow crystalline solid — what is it?
Sulfur (American spelling or sulphur (Commonwealth spelling) is a chemical element; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.

Proposed by Albert Einstein in special and general forms published in 1905 and 1915, this framework superseded 200-year-old Newtonian mechanics and explains gravitation's relation to the other forces of nature — name it?
Theory of relativity comprises two physics theories by Albert Einstein: special relativity and general relativity. Special relativity applies to all physical phenomena in the absence of gravity.

Native only to New Zealand and resembling a lizard, this reptile is the sole surviving member of an order that was hugely diverse in the Mesozoic era, with fossils dating to the Middle Triassic — what's the animal?
Tuatara (Mori:; Sphenodon punctatus) is a species of reptile endemic to New Zealand.
This Russian-American inventor built a television system using cathode-ray tubes and worked on image tubes and the electron microscope — who was he?
Vladimir K. Zworykin (1888/1889 - July 29, 1982) was a Russian-American inventor, engineer, and pioneer of television technology.

Native to freshwater and brackish habitats across western Eurasia, this ray-finned fish in the perch family, related to perch, ruffe, and darters, has become a popular game species well beyond its original range. Name it?
Zander (Sander lucioperca), sander or pikeperch, is a species of ray-finned fish from the family Percidae (which also includes perch, ruffe and darter).
Prescribed for ADHD and narcolepsy but also misused as a euphoriant, this fixed-dose pill packs four different amphetamine salts into one tablet. What is its brand name?
Adderall: Drug mixture used mainly to treat ADHD and narcolepsy.
This Scottish physician shared the 1945 Nobel Prize for discovering penicillin, and in 1922 identified an enzyme in his own nasal discharge — who is he?
Alexander Fleming: Scottish physician and microbiologist (1881–1955)
This inorganic salt, most commonly used as a soil fertilizer, is 21% nitrogen and 24% sulfur by content — what is it?
Known by the symbol Sb and mined chiefly from stibnite ore, which element has long been powdered into the cosmetic kohl and today hardens lead in car batteries?
Antimony: Chemical element with atomic number 51 (Sb)
His namesake effect — scattered X-rays losing energy — proved light behaves as particles and earned a share of the 1927 Nobel Prize in Physics. Who was this American physicist?
Nicknamed the hay bacterium for its soil habitat, this rod-shaped, spore-forming microbe is the best-studied Gram-positive species and a top industrial source of secreted enzymes — what is it?
Bacillus subtilis: Catalase-positive bacterium. It forms biofilms through the formation of extracellular polymeric matrix containing sugars and proteins.
This steroid medication treats everything from rheumatoid arthritis to psoriasis, and can even be given to speed a premature baby's lung development before birth — what is it?
Betamethasone: Steroid medication. It can be taken by mouth, injected into a muscle, or applied to the skin, typically in cream, lotion, or liquid forms.
Launched as the 7X7 program in 1978 and designed to complement the larger 747, which American wide-body airliner first entered service with United Airlines in 1982?
This Asian insect species, first found in Pennsylvania in 1998, cost Mid-Atlantic apple growers $37 million in a single year and now threatens hazelnut harvests worldwide — what is it?

Brown marmorated stink bug: Species of Pentatomid insect. The brown marmorated stink bug (Halyomorpha halys) is an insect in the family Pentatomidae, native to China, Japan, Korea, and other Asian regions.
Cultivated since China's Song Dynasty and boasting thousands of ornamental cultivars, which flowering shrub from the tea family is native to forests of China and Japan?
Camellia japonica: Species of flowering plant.
Nicknamed the pudding-pipe tree, this Fabaceae-family plant is the national tree of Thailand and doubles as the state flower of Kerala and Delhi — which species?

Cassia fistula: Species of flowering plant. Cassia fistula, also known as golden shower, purging cassia, Indian laburnum, kani konna, or pudding-pipe tree, is a flowering plant in the family Fabaceae.
Capable of sprinting up to 104 km/h, this spotted big cat is the fastest land animal alive, sporting black tear-like streaks down its face and a flexible spine built for speed — which animal?
Cheetah: Large feline of the genus Acinonyx.
Dubbed the 'father of information theory,' this polymath was the first to apply Boolean algebra to digital circuits and helped found the field of artificial intelligence — who is he?

Nocturnal and marked with narrow white crossbands on a bluish-black body, this South Asian snake's potent neurotoxic venom places it among the region's 'Big Four' most dangerous species — which snake?
Common krait: Species of snake. The common krait (Bungarus caeruleus) is a highly venomous snake species belonging to the genus Bungarus in the family Elapidae.
These feather-gilled freshwater crustaceans share their taxonomic order with lobsters and turn up in everything from brooks to rice paddies — what are they?
Crayfish: Freshwater crustaceans. Crayfish are freshwater crustaceans belonging to the infraorder Astacidea, which also contains lobsters.
The first Western European combat aircraft to break Mach 2 in level flight, achieving the feat in October 1958, which French fighter jet family was this?
Dassault Mirage III: French supersonic fighter/interceptor aircraft.

Discovered in Arizona in the 1940s and first classified as a species of Megalosaurus, this theropod was reassigned to a new genus in 1970 once paleontologists noticed the twin crests on its skull — which dinosaur?
Dilophosaurus: Genus of theropod dinosaur from the Early Jurassic.

Coined by Robert Spitzer in the late 1970s to replace the notion of a "depressive personality," this condition resembles major depression but lingers for at least two years — and now goes by "persistent depressive disorder." What was its original name?
Dysthymia: Psychiatric disorder defined by chronic depression.
Caused by viruses like herpes simplex or rabies, this inflammation of the brain can bring fever, confusion, and a stiff neck — what is this condition?

Encephalitis: Inflammation of the brain. The severity can be variable with symptoms including reduction or alteration in consciousness, aphasia, headache, fever, confusion, a stiff neck, and vomiting.
This complex-analysis identity states that e raised to the power of ix equals cosine x plus i times sine x, linking exponential and trigonometric functions — what is it called?
Euler's formula: Complex exponential in terms of sine and cosine. The formula is still valid if x is a complex number, and is also called Euler's formula in this more general case.
Carnivora splits into two suborders, dog-like and cat-like — which one groups cats, hyenas, mongooses, and viverrids together?
Found at the end of the leg and typically featuring claws or nails, which weight-bearing body part enables locomotion in many vertebrates?
Foot: Anatomical structure found in vertebrates.

In 1974 in Pacific Grove, California, this computer scientist demoed the first working prototype of CP/M and invented the BIOS, then founded Digital Research to sell his software — who was this PC-revolution pioneer?
Gary Kildall: American computer scientist and microcomputer entrepreneur (1942–1994)

Making up about 15% of all brain tumors and thought to arise from cells called astrocytes, this aggressive cancer often announces itself only with vague headaches or sudden personality changes — what is it?
Glioblastoma: Aggressive type of brain cancer. Initial signs and symptoms of glioblastoma are nonspecific.
Closely related to the llama, this wild South American camelid shares its range with a higher-altitude cousin, the vicuña — what is it?
Named for the Greek word for the sun, this element makes up about 24% of the universe's elemental mass and has the lowest boiling point of all — which colorless, odorless gas?
Helium: Chemical element with atomic number 2 (He)
German anthropologist Otto Schoetensack named this archaic human species in 1908 based on a jawbone found near the village of Mauer — then Europe's oldest known human fossil. Which species?

Homo heidelbergensis: Extinct species of archaic human. H. heidelbergensis has been regarded as either the last common ancestor of modern humans, Neanderthals, and Denisovans; or as a completely separate lineage.
A person with this condition becomes unduly alarmed by even the most minor symptom, convinced a serious illness is upon them despite no medical diagnosis — what is it?
Hypochondriasis: Excessive fear of developing illness.
This cerebrovascular condition is a localized ballooning of a brain blood vessel most often found in the Circle of Willis, with the 'berry'-shaped type being the most common. What is it?

Intracranial aneurysm: Ballooning or rupturing of a blood vessel in the brain. The risk of rupture varies with the size and location of the aneurysm, with those in the posterior circulation being more prone to rupture.
After a cross-country road trip from New York to Seattle, this Princeton engineering graduate founded an online bookstore in 1994 that grew into a global e-commerce giant. Who is he?

This Indian aerospace engineer led the nation's space agency as chairman and served as secretary of the Department of Space, after directing both the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre and the Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre — who is he?
Once a water retriever in Italy's Po Delta marshlands, this Italian dog breed later became prized for sniffing out truffles — which breed?
Lagotto Romagnolo: Italian breed of dog.
As a principal shareholder of L'Oréal, this French heiress was the richest woman in the world at the time of her death in 2017, worth $44.3 billion — who was she?
Liliane Bettencourt: French heiress, socialite and businesswoman (1922–2017)
Originating in 1993 and written in ANSI C, this lightweight scripting language was designed to be embedded inside other applications — which language?
Lua: Lightweight programming language. Lua is a lightweight, high-level, multi-paradigm programming language designed mainly for embedded use in applications.
Oblate rather than round, with a thin, loose peel that makes it easy to separate into segments, this citrus fruit is sweeter and stronger-tasting than its spherical, hybrid cousin — which fruit?
Mandarin orange: Small citrus fruit. A mandarin orange (Citrus reticulata), often simply called mandarin, is a small, rounded citrus tree fruit.
This small, highly social mongoose from southern Africa lives in packs of up to 30, with a dominance hierarchy where usually only the top pair breeds. What animal is it?
Meerkat: Species of mongoose from Southern Africa. The meerkat (Suricata suricatta) or suricate is a small mongoose found in southern Africa.

This medical condition, usually diagnosed shortly after birth, is defined as a length at least 2.5 standard deviations below the average and affects about 1.5 in 10,000 male newborns in North America. What is this condition?
The platypus and the four species of echidna are the only living mammals in this order that lay eggs rather than bear live young — what is it called?

This inner-ear condition brings on episodes of vertigo, ringing in the ears, and hearing loss lasting anywhere from 20 minutes to several hours — believed to stem from fluid buildup in the labyrinth. What is it?
Ménière's disease: Disorder of the inner ear. The hearing loss and ringing in the ears can become constant over time.
Present in 26 African countries with one of its largest undisturbed populations at Kenya's Lake Turkana, which large crocodilian sees adult males reach 3.5 to 5 metres long?
This British engineer rewrote Maxwell's equations into the form we use today and devised the telegrapher's equations — who was he?
Oliver Heaviside: British mathematician and electrical engineer (1850–1925)
Discovered in 1802 and named after a newly found asteroid, this silvery-white platinum-group metal is prized for cleaning up automobile exhaust in catalytic converters — which element?
Palladium: Chemical element with atomic number 46 (Pd)

Caused by a lack of vitamin B3 (niacin), this disease is remembered for its grim quartet of symptoms — inflamed skin, diarrhea, dementia, and mouth sores — striking sun-exposed skin first. What is it?
Pellagra: Human disease caused by a lack of vitamin B3. The two main types of pellagra are primary and secondary.
With the formula H3PO4, this colorless, odorless compound is typically sold as an 85% aqueous solution and serves as a key ingredient in many fertilizers — what is it?

Its methods range from gentle negotiation and lawmaking all the way to warfare against adversaries, and the social science that studies it tacks 'science' onto its name; what is this activity of settling a society's affairs?
Politics: Activities associated with group decisions.

Built from long chains of amino acid residues, these biomolecules fold into specific 3D shapes that catalyze reactions, copy DNA, and ferry molecules around the cell. What are these workhorse macromolecules?
Protein: Biomolecule consisting of chains of amino acid residues.
The sole member of its genus and a relative of apples and pears, this hard, aromatic golden fruit is too tart to enjoy raw but turns lovely as jam or a fragrant cheese — what is it?
With the widest geographic range of any non-human primate, this brown-to-grey Old World monkey lives in matrilineal troops of up to 200 individuals — which species?
Rhesus macaque: Species of Old World monkey. The rhesus macaque (Macaca mulatta), colloquially rhesus monkey, is a species of Old World monkey in the Macaca genus.
What term describes herbivorous mammals like cattle and giraffes that digest plant matter by regurgitating and re-chewing it as cud?
Ruminant: Hoofed herbivorous grazing or browsing mammals.
In this thought experiment a hypothetical cat in a closed box may be considered simultaneously alive and dead. Which quantum concept is it illustrating?
In quantum mechanics, Schrödinger's cat is a thought experiment concerning quantum superposition, in which a hypothetical cat in a closed box may be considered simultaneously alive and dead.
Called the 'father of modern differential geometry,' this Chinese-born American mathematician and poet was honored with a medal the IMU named after him in 2010 — who is he?

Shiing-Shen Chern: Chinese-American mathematician and poet. Shiing-Shen Chern (Chinese: 陳省身; pinyin: Chén Xǐngshēn; October 26, 1911 – December 3, 2004) was a Chinese-born American mathematician and poet.

Native to Eurasia and found in Paleolithic-era deposits in ancient Britain, this flowering plant's ripe berries and cooked leaves are eaten in some regions despite its nightshade family's fearsome reputation — what is it?
Solanum nigrum: Species of flowering plant in the nightshade family. The plant was known and mentioned by ancient herbalists, including Dioscorides.
This Taiwanese-American engineer co-founded YouTube and served as its CTO before later building the video app MixBit — who is he?
Native to the Balkan Peninsula, this fragrant flowering shrub in the olive family is cultivated widely across Europe and North America for its clusters of purple or white blooms — which species?
Syringa vulgaris: Plant species in the olive family.

This rare chromosomal condition gives affected females four copies of a single chromosome instead of the usual two, and is linked to distinctive facial features and skeletal quirks like incurved pinky fingers — what is it called?
Tetrasomy X: Chromosomal disorder with 4 X chromosomes.
These digits let cats walk in a 'digitigrade' stance, while humans are 'plantigrade,' resting on the soles of their feet instead — what are they?
Nicknamed 'Blinder' by NATO, this disappointing supersonic bomber was still exported to Libya and Iraq, seeing combat against Tanzania and in the Iran–Iraq War — which aircraft?
Tupolev Tu-22: Soviet supersonic heavy bomber.
Similar in size and mass to Earth, this planet has an atmosphere far thicker and denser than any other rocky body in the Solar System — and none of what?

Venus is the second planet from the Sun. Similar in size and mass to Earth, Venus has no liquid water, and its atmosphere is far thicker and denser than that of any other rocky body in the Solar System.
Packing a mass comparable to the Sun into a volume the size of Earth, this dense stellar remnant glows from leftover heat rather than nuclear fusion — what is it?
White dwarf: Stellar core remnant. A white dwarf is a very dense type of star: in an Earth-sized volume, it packs a mass that is comparable to the Sun.
Known by the formula ZnO, this white, water-insoluble powder shows up in sunscreens, calamine lotion, and rubber manufacturing — which compound?
Zinc oxide: White powder insoluble in water. Although it occurs naturally as the mineral zincite, most zinc oxide is produced synthetically.

The symbol for zinc is Zn. Zinc is a chemical element; it has symbol Zn and atomic number 30.

Dwayne Johnson: Dwayne Douglas Johnson (born May 2, 1972), also known by his ring name "The Rock", is an American actor and professional wrestler.
